subject.title: [Feature]: Automatic Output Sanitization for Sensitive Data

question: Should OpenClaw add a core automatic final-output sanitization policy/config surface, route this to plugin hooks or ClawHub packages, or keep the current log/transcript/tool redaction boundary only?
rationale: The requested behavior changes what users see and what channels deliver, and it adds security-sensitive config/default policy that cannot be selected safely from source inspection alone.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core design
options.body: Define the final-output boundary, default mode, false-positive rules, and upgrade behavior before implementing a bounded core sanitizer that reuses existing redaction helpers where appropriate.

options.title: Route to plugin or ClawHub
options.body: Use message_sending/reply_payload_sending hooks for optional sanitizer packages, accepting that this will not be an automatic core default.

options.title: Keep current boundary
options.body: Decline final-output sanitization for now and continue hardening log, transcript, diagnostic, and tool-payload redaction only.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow core design
recommendation.body: Define the final-output boundary, default mode, false-positive rules, and upgrade behavior before implementing a bounded core sanitizer that reuses existing redaction helpers where appropriate.

likelyOwner.reason: He has recent history on the outbound sanitization boundary and logging/config documentation, and is the best available code-history routing candidate for the security/config product choice.
